text:
Alex K.: noticing a spike in login failures starting ~09:04 UTC, console 403 for some users. Auth checks failing with token verification errors against Auth0 EU jwks endpoint. paging now.
Nina (incident-bot): Incident created: IN-2350 auth-provider-token-verify-eu (severity: P2) — paging eng-oncall.
Samir R.: I'm on it. can someone paste an example error from prod logs?
Alex K.: stack traces: `TokenVerifierError: no matching kid` and `jwks fetch failed 502`. snippet:
```
ERROR auth.verify token=abc123 user_id=... err="jwks fetch failed: 502 Bad Gateway"
WARN auth.verify token=def456 err="no matching kid in cached keys"
```
Morgan D.: customers reporting console login 403s and some API calls 401. impact: ~4% of auth traffic in eu-west-1, higher for EU customers. metrics dashboard: spike in `auth.verify.errors` + `auth.http.403` starting 09:04.
Jamie L.: can we short-circuit to cached keys and bypass real-time jwks fetch? what's the current jwks cache TTL?
Samir R.: TTL currently 5m. cache appears to be invalidated when fetch fails. immediate mitigation: set fallback to use last-known-good keys and extend TTL to 1h while AWS/Auth0 incident is ongoing. rolling change, low-risk.
Alex K.: agree. Samir, can you push a quick config change via feature flag? we have a runtime flag `auth.jwks.fallback_mode=on` that uses cached set and disables fetch.
Samir R.: applying now.
deploy-bot: Started rollout of feature-flag auth.jwks.fallback_mode -> on (canary 3 -> 10%).
Samir R.: canaries look good, no error spike. increasing to 100% now.
deploy-bot: Rollout complete. auth.jwks.fallback_mode = on across eu clusters.
Alex K.: monitoring. initial effect: 403 rate down from 4% -> 0.6% in 10m. good.
Morgan D.: customer inbound: support ticket #2345 from AcmeCorp (EU) - login failures for users in germany. sent a note to affected customers: "We're experiencing degraded login for some EU users; we've applied fallback to reduce impact; full resolution pending with provider."
Jamie L.: next mitigation: add warning in console UI for re-auth to reduce support load? maybe surface an alert banner. product approves?
Morgan D.: yes, small banner: "We're experiencing login disruptions for some EU users; you may be asked to re-login." i'll coordinate with ux.
Samir R.: digging into why cache was invalidated: fetch returned 502 and we have aggressive retry logic that rotates keys out. will patch retry/backoff and remove purge on transient fetch failures.
Alex K.: assign a follow-up ticket for the retry/backoff fix and increase default cache TTL for eu region.
Samir R.: created TASK-7212: "Add transient-failure guard to jwks cache purging + backoff tuning" and linked incident.
Nina (incident-bot): Handoff requested — current oncall needs to go. paging night oncall in 30m.
Alex K.: i'm handing off to Samir for overnight monitoring. summary: Auth0 EU jwks endpoint returned 502 causing key fetch fail and token verify errors -> we enabled auth.jwks.fallback_mode using cached keys; blocked purge on transient failures; customer-facing banner deployed; monitoring shows error rate back down to baseline.
Samir R.: taking handoff. will watch dashboards and escalate to Auth0 if provider status doesn't improve in 1h. I'll also reach out to partners channel for any cross-team auth infra impact.
Jamie L.: product to draft postmortem content — any suggested customer messaging? short note + post-incident followup with root cause and our mitigation steps.
Alex K.: suggested message: "We experienced intermittent login failures for some EU customers due to a third-party identity provider outage. We applied a server-side fallback to cached keys and adjusted our retry behavior to mitigate recurrence. We're monitoring and will follow up with details."
Morgan D.: support notified and CS is triaging high-severity customers.
Samir R.: next steps posted to incident doc, will update if Auth0 posts maint/update. handing off active watch to night oncall at 00:00 UTC.
Nina (incident-bot): Incident status changed to: "Mitigated - monitoring".
Alex K.: thanks team — good quick mitigation. root cause likely provider transient error; we'll keep TASK-7212 and follow up in postmortem.
